questions.question: Sir Tim Berners-Lee is associated with
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**World Wide Web**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sir Tim Berners-Lee is credited with the invention of the **World Wide Web** in 1989 while working at CERN (European Organization for Nuclear Research).
 
• He developed the first web browser named **WorldWideWeb (later renamed Nexus)** and introduced the concept of URLs, HTTP, and HTML, which are the building blocks of the web.
 
• The World Wide Web revolutionized the way people access and share information globally, creating the foundation for the modern internet.
 
• He also founded the **World Wide Web Consortium (W3C)** in 1994, which develops web standards to ensure that the web remains accessible to everyone.
 
• Tim Berners-Lee has been recognized for his contributions with numerous accolades, including being knighted by Queen Elizabeth II in 2004 and receiving the Turing Award in 2016.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **GUI Concept:**
 
 
• **Graphical User Interface (GUI)** allows users to interact with computers using visual elements such as icons, windows, and menus rather than text-based commands.
 
• It was popularized by Xerox PARC and later adopted by companies like Apple and Microsoft in their operating systems.
 
• While Sir Tim Berners-Lee did not directly contribute to the development of GUI, it played a vital role in making computers user-friendly and accessible to the general public.
 
 
 
• **ATM:**
 
 
• **Automated Teller Machines (ATMs)** were invented by John Shepherd-Barron in 1967 and are used for banking services such as cash withdrawal and balance inquiry.
 
• ATMs operate using a secure PIN system and magnetic stripe cards, later upgraded to chip-based cards for added security.
 
• The invention of ATMs revolutionized banking by providing customers with 24/7 access to their accounts.
 
 
 
• **Microprocessor:**
 
 
• The microprocessor is the central component of a computer system, acting as its brain. It was invented by **Intel engineers Federico Faggin, Ted Hoff, and Stan Mazor** in 1971.
 
• The first commercially available microprocessor was the Intel 4004, which paved the way for advancements in computing technology.
 
• Microprocessors are used in various devices, including computers, smartphones, and embedded systems.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme:**
 
 
• The World Wide Web (WWW) is distinct from the internet, which refers to the network infrastructure connecting computers globally.
 
• The web is a service that operates on the internet, enabling users to view and interact with web pages via browsers.
 
• Tim Berners-Lee's invention of the web laid the foundation for e-commerce, social media, and countless other applications that have transformed modern society.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: When was Chandrayaan-I launched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2008**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Chandrayaan-I was India’s first lunar probe and was launched by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) on **22 October 2008**.
 
• The spacecraft was launched aboard the **PSLV-C11**, a modified version of ISRO’s Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle.
 
• The mission was designed to study the Moon through high-resolution remote sensing in visible, near-infrared, and X-ray wavelengths.
 
• Chandrayaan-I’s significant achievement was the discovery of **water molecules on the lunar surface**, which was a major milestone in space exploration.
 
• The mission ended on 29 August 2009 after contact with the spacecraft was lost, but it was considered a success as it achieved 95% of its mission objectives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandrayaan Missions**

 
 
• The Chandrayaan program is a series of lunar exploration missions conducted by ISRO to advance India’s capabilities in space science and technology.
 
• Following the success of Chandrayaan-I, ISRO launched Chandrayaan-II in 2019, which included an orbiter, a lander (Vikram), and a rover (Pragyan).
 
• These missions aim to explore the Moon’s surface, study its composition, and enhance our understanding of the lunar environment.

questions.question: The concept known as Shor’s Algorithm is primarily associated with which one of the following technological domains?

options.text: Secure military communication systems based on satellite networks
High-speed financial data transmission between banking institutions
Algorithms used in next-generation quantum computing for solving complex mathematical problems
Advanced missile interception and defence mechanisms

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option C**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shor’s Algorithm** is a landmark development in the field of **quantum computing**, demonstrating the potential of quantum algorithms to outperform classical algorithms for certain problems.
 
• It is especially significant because it addresses **computationally hard mathematical problems** that underpin modern cryptographic systems.
 
• **Shor’s Algorithm** is designed to efficiently solve problems such as **integer factorisation** and **discrete logarithms** using **quantum bits (qubits)** and quantum parallelism, which are infeasible to solve efficiently on classical computers. **Hence, Option C is correct. **
 
• The algorithm is **not related** to satellite-based military communications, financial data transmission systems, or missile defence technologies. **Hence, Options A, B, and D are incorrect. **

**Thus, the correct answer is → Option C. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Shor’s Algorithm poses a theoretical threat to widely used **public-key cryptographic systems** such as **RSA**.
 
• It relies on quantum principles like **superposition** and **quantum Fourier transform**.
 
• Practical implementation requires **large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computers**, which are still under development.
 
• The algorithm was proposed in **1994** and is considered a foundation of **quantum algorithm research**.

questions.question: Which type of nuclear radiation has highest ionising power but least penetrating ability?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option A. **

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alpha radiation consists of helium nuclei (two protons and two neutrons), **making the particles heavy and positively charged. This causes intense interaction with matter over a very short distance.** Hence, Option A is correct. **
 
• Because of their** large mass and charge, alpha particles lose energy rapidly and therefore have the highest ionising power among common nuclear radiations**. **Hence, Alpha radiation has the highest ionising power.**
 
• However, the same properties result in very low penetrating ability; alpha particles can be stopped by a sheet of paper, human skin, or a few centimetres of air. **Hence, alpha radiation has the least penetration. **
 
• Beta radiation has moderate ionising and penetrating power, while gamma rays and neutrons have very high penetrating power but comparatively lower ionising power per unit path length**. Hence, Options B, C, and D are incorrect. **

**Thus, the radiation with highest ionising power but least penetrating ability → Option A. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ionising power refers to the ability of radiation to remove electrons from atoms or molecules.
 
• Penetrating power refers to how deeply radiation can pass through matter.
 
• Order of ionising power:** Alpha > Beta > Gamma **
 
• Order of penetrating power**: Gamma > Beta > Alpha **
 
• Alpha radiation is especially dangerous when inhaled or ingested, as it can cause severe internal tissue damage despite being easily stopped externally.

questions.question: Which among the following are India's permanent and operational research stations in Antarctica?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharati and Maitri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **__Confusion Points__** 

__
 
• As of today, India has two operational research stations in Antarctica named Maitri and Bharati.
 
• Dakshin Gangotri was the first scientific base station of India situated in Antarctica, part of the Indian Antarctic Programme. **It is not** operational.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• The Indian Antarctic expeditions began in 1981. The first trip comprised a team of 21 scientists and support staff led by Dr. SZ Qasim. After a humble beginning, the Indian Antarctic programme has now been credited to have built three permanent research base stations in Antarctica—named Dakshin Gangotri, Maitri, and Bharati.
 
• **Bharati and Maitri** are India's permanent and operational research stations in Antarctica.
 
• **Maitri Research Station**:
 
 
• It was built and finished in 1989, shortly before the first station Dakshin Gangotri was buried in ice and got abandoned in 1990–91. It is not operational now.
 
• It is currently being used as a supply base and transit camp.
 
• The base is named after Dakshin Gangotri Glacier. It was established during the third Indian expedition to Antarctica in 1983–84.
 
• Maitri Research Station is in the rocky mountainous region of Antarctica, called Schirmacher Oasis.
 
• I**t is equipped with modern technology and facilities which are used to research in various fields such as earth science, meteorology, glaciology, etc.**
 
 
 
• **Bharati Research Station**:
 
 
• It is India's third Antarctic research facility and one of two active Indian research stations, alongside Maitri.
 
• **The mandate focuses on oceanographic studies and the phenomenon of continental breakup.**
 
• It also facilitates research to refine the current understanding of the Indian subcontinent's geological history.
